articles.title: The Trump-Putin alliance threatens every European country – yet gushing populists still cheer them | Steve Bloomfield
articles.summary:
Europe’s future will be fought over at the ballot box and on Ukraine’s frontline. The danger is that the two strongmen ultimately reap the benefits

On the facade of Stenbock House, the Estonian prime minister’s neoclassical office building on a hill in Tallinn, sits a plaque commemorating the murder of 10 heads of government. They were all killed by Soviet forces after the USSR’s invasion of Estonia in 1940.

For 51 years, Estonia was occupied by its imperial neighbour; for the past 25 years it has lived independently in its shadow. For the politicians and government officials who work at Stenbock House, the plaque is a constant reminder of the risk the small Baltic nation (population 1.4 million) faces from a neighbour 100 times its size.

Steve Bloomfield is a Guardian international affairs commentator
